findings.reader: A well-executed dated news report: it answers what Muse can do now, makes the agent-to-permission-to-service chain visible in unbranded plain language, and cleanly separates today's policy-limited Meta access from the promised but unavailable user-held-key privacy mode. Terms are defined in context, vendor claims stay attributed, uncertainty survives to the ending, and the closing advice is specific and proportionate. No failure families present.
findings.facts: Fact-checking finds the article faithful to its three sources: launch facts, permission mechanics, fallibility admissions and the current-versus-promised privacy boundary all match the Meta launch post, Meta safety post and AP observation with attribution intact. One claim (the recipe/invitation email framing) is a reasonable composed inference rather than verbatim sourcing, marked qualified. Dates, limits and uncertainty are handled correctly; no contradictions or unreviewable claims.
